stem.text: A particle moves along the curve \( x^{3} + x y^{2} = 10 \) so that its coordinates \( x \) and \( y \) are differentiable functions of time \( t \). At the instant the particle is at the point \( (1, 3) \), \( \frac{dy}{dt} = -2 \) units per second. Find \( \frac{dx}{dt} \), in units per second, at that instant.

worked_solution.text: Differentiate both sides of \( x^{3} + x y^{2} = 10 \) with respect to \( t \), using the product rule on the term that contains both variables: \( \left(3 x^{2} + y^{2}\right)\frac{dx}{dt} + \left(2 x y\right)\frac{dy}{dt} = 0 \).
At \( (1, 3) \) the coefficient of \( \frac{dy}{dt} \) is \( 6 \) and the coefficient of \( \frac{dx}{dt} \) is \( 12 \). Substitute \( \frac{dy}{dt} = -2 \): \( (6)(-2) + (12)\frac{dx}{dt} = 0 \).
